import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as ui from '../support/ui';

test.setTimeout(240_000);
test.describe("statement lines", () => {
  test("statement lines", { tag: '@functionality' }, async ({ browser }) => {
    const sheet = ui.sheetId();
    const pg_uma = await ui.userPage(browser, "uma", sheet);
    await ui.setToday(pg_uma, "2026-03-10");
    expect(await ui.setRate(pg_uma, {"grade": "A", "pct": "10.00"})).toBe(true);
    const p_ada = ui.must(await ui.addPerson(pg_uma, {"name": "Ada", "grade": "A"}));
    expect(await ui.setRole(pg_uma, "vic", "steward")).toBe(true);
    const c_ada_0 = ui.must(await ui.addClaim(pg_uma, p_ada, {"amount": "10.00"}));
    expect(await ui.claimAction(pg_uma, c_ada_0, "open")).toBe(true);
    expect(await ui.statement(pg_uma, p_ada)).toBe(true);
    expect(await ui.setRate(pg_uma, {"grade": "A", "pct": "20.00"})).toBe(true);
    await ui.setToday(pg_uma, "2026-03-11");
    expect(await ui.statement(pg_uma, p_ada)).toBe(true);
    const c_ada_1 = ui.must(await ui.addClaim(pg_uma, p_ada, {"amount": "5.00"}));
    expect(await ui.claimAction(pg_uma, c_ada_1, "open")).toBe(true);
    await ui.setToday(pg_uma, "2026-03-12");
    expect(await ui.statementAsOf(pg_uma, p_ada, "2026-03-11")).toBe(true);
    await ui.refresh(pg_uma);
    await expect(pg_uma.getByTestId("person-row-" + p_ada).getByTestId("person-statement-line-line")).toHaveText(["2026-03-10 1.00", "2026-03-11 1.00", "2026-03-11 2.00"]);

    await expect(pg_uma.getByTestId("person-row-" + p_ada).getByTestId("person-statement-date")).toHaveText("2026-03-11");
    await expect(pg_uma.getByTestId("claim-row-" + c_ada_1).getByTestId("claim-stated")).toHaveText("yes");

    await expect(pg_uma.getByTestId("claim-row-" + c_ada_0).getByTestId("claim-stated")).toHaveText("yes");
    await expect(pg_uma.getByTestId("claim-row-" + c_ada_0).getByTestId("claim-due")).toHaveText("1.00");
    const pg_vic = await ui.userPage(browser, "vic", sheet);
    expect(await ui.unstate(pg_vic, p_ada)).toBe(true);
    await ui.refresh(pg_vic);
    await expect(pg_vic.getByTestId("person-row-" + p_ada).getByTestId("person-statement-line-line")).toHaveText(["2026-03-10 1.00", "2026-03-11 1.00"]);
    await expect(pg_vic.getByTestId("person-row-" + p_ada).getByTestId("person-statement-count")).toHaveText("2");
    await expect(pg_vic.getByTestId("person-row-" + p_ada).getByTestId("person-stated-total")).toHaveText("1.00");
    await expect(pg_vic.getByTestId("person-row-" + p_ada).getByTestId("person-statement-date")).toHaveText("2026-03-11");
    await expect(pg_vic.getByTestId("claim-row-" + c_ada_1).getByTestId("claim-stated")).toHaveText("no");
    await expect(pg_vic.getByTestId("claim-row-" + c_ada_1).getByTestId("claim-due")).toHaveText("1.00");

    ]);

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build, start the whole app, run the Playwright specs present in e2e/specs, then stop.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

# Refuse to run against a server that is not ours: an app left running on $PORT (an earlier
# bin/start that was never stopped, another sandbox) would take the tests and fail them all.
if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "bin/e2e: something is already serving on port ${PORT}; stop it (bin/stop) or set PORT to a free port" >&2
  exit 2
fi

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL. A loaded
# machine can take minutes to bring the JVM up; running the specs before it is ready fails every
# one of them for no reason, so wait long and fail loudly rather than run against nothing.
ready=0
for i in $(seq 1 300); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ready=1; break; fi
  sleep 1
done
if [ "$ready" != 1 ]; then
  echo "bin/e2e: the app did not become healthy on port ${PORT} within 300s; see .run/app.log" >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Install deps + the Chromium browser (both cached after first run), then run the specs.
( cd e2e && npm ci --silent && npx --yes playwright install chromium && npx playwright test )
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start the Spring Boot app on $PORT (main class net.officefloor.hq.app.Application). On boot, Flyway
# migrates the empty in-memory H2 up to the current schema; Spring serves the SPA (static/) and the
# app's REST endpoints. Returns once
# launching; poll /actuator/health for readiness.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
mkdir -p .run

: "${PORT:?PORT must be set}"
JAR="$(ls -t target/*.jar 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
[ -n "$JAR" ] || { echo "no jar in target/ — run bin/build first" >&2; exit 1; }

# Known audit file (the file-based test-assertion channel). Absolute so app + tests agree.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

nohup java -jar "$JAR" --server.port="$PORT" --spring.profiles.active=e2e > .run/app.log 2>&1 &
echo $! > .run/app.pid
// Playwright config. Tests bind to data-testid only and assert through the UI. The app is already
// running (started by bin/e2e), so no webServer here.
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: './specs',
  use: {
    baseURL: process.env.BASE_URL ?? `http://localhost:${process.env.PORT ?? 3000}`,
    // The contract attribute is data-testid — Playwright's default, so no testIdAttribute override
    // needed. Strict awaiting on data-testid presence is the flake guard.
  },
  // Every spec arranges its own data through the screens on a sheet id of its own and reads the
  // audit file filtered by that id, so specs never share data. workers:1 keeps the suite serial
  // against the one shared app, so a failure stays attributable to one spec.
  fullyParallel: false,
  workers: 1,
  reporter: [['list']],
  projects: [
    {
      name: 'chromium',
      use: {
        ...devices['Desktop Chrome'],
        // Headless Chromium needs its own sandbox off and
        // shared memory in /tmp, or renderer/GPU child processes crash. Harmless elsewhere too.
        launchOptions: { args: ['--no-sandbox', '--disable-dev-shm-usage', '--disable-gpu'] },
      },
    },
  ],
});
# OfficeHQ

A full-stack office-management web application.

- **Front end:** Angular single-page app (standalone components, lazy routes), built into
  `src/main/resources/static`.
- **Back end:** Spring Boot with Spring MVC `@RestController` endpoints, on an in-memory H2 database
  with Flyway migrations run on boot.

## Build and run

```
bin/build              # build the SPA and package one runnable jar
PORT=3000 bin/start    # start the app (serves the SPA + REST on $PORT)
bin/stop               # stop it
```

Readiness: `GET /actuator/health`.

## Tests

End-to-end tests use Playwright (in `e2e/`) and bind to `data-testid`:

```
bin/e2e                # build, start, run the specs in e2e/specs, then stop
```

I've added the statement lines, and three of the four `bin/e2e` tests pass. "statement lines scenario 2" still fails, and the cause is the machine's clock, not this change.

**The change**
- **Server:** `StatementSummary` now builds one line per stored statement. A cancelled statement is deleted from the store, so it drops out on its own. Lines are sorted oldest first by the date each statement shows: its as-of date, else the day it was taken. Statements on the same date stay in the order they were taken. Statements brought over by a merge or transfer are sorted in by date along with the person's own. `PersonView` sends these lines as `statements`, including in the as-of view rebuilt from history.
- **Front end:** each person row has a new "Statement lines" column. Each line is a `person-statement-line-line` element showing `<date> <due-total>`, or `n/a` when the due-total wasn't available, the same way snapshot lines work.

**Why scenario 2 fails**
The test makes a parent sheet (`<sheet>-p`) and never sets its "today". A new sheet's today defaults to the real date (`LocalDate.now()` in `SheetService.java:36`), which is 2026-11-15. The parent's rates are therefore recorded on 2026-11-15. When the test views the child sheet as of 2026-03-20, the parent's rates don't exist yet, so grade C shows `n/a` where the test expects the parent's 12.50 (and a claim due of 1.29).
